newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais, U.S. discuss communications satellite use.
newsitem.headline: Thais, U.S. discuss communications satellite use.

text.p: Thailand is holding discussions with the United States on the use of American defence satellites for communications purposes, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Tuesday.
Preliminary talks between the Thai defence ministry and the United States had been held and further discussions were needed for the deal to be completed, he told reporters.
"Further discussions need to be held on this issue," Chavalit said when asked about the plan to use the satellites. He did not give further details.
A U.S. embassy spokesman told Reuters the U.S. Department of Defence had held preliminary discussions with the Thai government regarding the capabilities and availability of existing satellites.
A U.S. defence team visited Thailand last week to discuss this issue further.
"As discussions on the possible cooperation are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to speculate on their outcome," the spokesman said when pressed for more details.
A Thai newspaper, the Bangkok Post, earlier this week quoting a defence ministry source as saying the United States was "very likely" to allow Thailand to use two of its defence satellites for free.
The source was reported as having said the United States seemed willing to help the Thai armed forces which had asked for the unconditional use of America's reserve satellites.
Thailand's military had originally planned to spend up to 26 billion baht ($1.04 billion) to acquire a spy and communications satellite system.
But opposition from politicians and senior government officials to the idea, which they said would be wasteful spending, caused the plan to be shelved.
Diplomatic sources said the alternative idea of leasing the American defence satellites for communications purposes was then seriously discussed.
The sources said that Thailand would then need to build a relay station, estimated to cost about three billion baht, to enable it to use the American satellites.

Some Thai newspapers reported that the United States might be ready to offer the Thais the use of the defence satellites at no cost. But an official at the U.S. Embassy said governments would generally want remuneration for such use by any party.
